title: <Teleport>: DOM Relocation Outside Component Root & Dynamic Targets

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine a nested Russian doll. If the smallest doll inside tries to open a giant umbrella (a modal), the umbrella gets crushed inside the tiny doll's shell. `<Teleport>` beams the umbrella straight out of the doll's belly and attaches it to the ceiling of the entire room (`<body>`), so it can open to full size without getting trapped.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `<Teleport to="body">` moves its template markup to a different DOM node (like `document.body` or `#modals-container`) while maintaining its reactive component connection. It is the standard solution for modals, tooltips, and notifications to prevent them from being cut off by parent CSS `overflow: hidden` or `z-index` stacking contexts. The `disabled` prop lets you toggle teleportation dynamically.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `<Teleport>` decouples physical DOM rendering from the virtual component hierarchy. The teleported content remains a child of the parent component in the Vue Virtual DOM tree: props, reactive state, `provide`/`inject`, and parent-child event listeners continue to function seamlessly. Teleport supports dynamic targets (`:to="target"`), multiple teleports targeting the same container (appended in order), and SSR hydration matching.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In `@vue/runtime-core`, Teleport is an internal built-in component with custom `process()` methods. When mounted, the renderer creates anchor comment nodes (`<!--teleport start-->` and `<!--teleport end-->`) in the original parent DOM position to mark its virtual slot. The actual child DOM nodes are inserted into the target DOM element resolved by `document.querySelector(to)`. When updating, the renderer patches elements inside the target container.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if the target element specified in `<Teleport to="#modal">` does not exist in the DOM when the component mounts?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of mounting order and querySelector timing.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: If the target element does not exist in the DOM when the component mounts, Vue will throw a runtime warning (`[Vue warn]: Failed to locate Teleport target with selector...`) and rendering of the teleported content will fail. The target DOM element must already exist in the HTML *before* the component containing `<Teleport>` is mounted.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not attempt to teleport to a sibling element that renders later in the same template; target elements must already be present in the DOM (e.g. in `index.html` or a previously mounted layout).

interviewGotchas.question: How does native DOM event bubbling behave for elements inside `<Teleport>` in Vue 3 vs React Portals?
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: In Vue 3, **native DOM events bubble through the physical HTML DOM tree**, following the target's new position in the DOM. (This differs from React Portals, where synthetic events bubble through the virtual component tree). However, Vue component custom events (`$emit`) still propagate through the Vue component hierarchy as expected.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: A native `@click` on the parent container in Vue will *not* catch clicks from teleported elements if they were moved outside that container in the physical DOM.
